headline: Good sleep helps, but keep the recovery day
summary: Recovery markers improved markedly after two quiet days, but the marathon and Monday's extra 7 km are still the dominant training signals. Keep today as a rest day and reassess normal walking, stairs and tendon response before considering a short run tomorrow.

recovery.label: Sleep
recovery.context: Good sleep with excellent duration; average sleep stress was 20 (fair).

recovery.label: Sleeping HR
recovery.context: Available in the raw sleep record, but historical sleeping-HR baselines were missing because of a collector field mismatch.

recovery.label: Resting HR
recovery.context: 3 bpm above the current seven-day average of 59.

recovery.label: Overnight HRV
recovery.context: Garmin rated the HRV contribution very good.

recovery.label: Body Battery
recovery.context: Up 64 points overnight; 46 at the mid-afternoon snapshot.

recovery.label: Training Readiness
recovery.context: Boosted by good sleep; about 24h 34m of recovery time remained.

yesterday.title: Rest day
yesterday.summary: No running activity was recorded. The quiet day allowed Body Battery and Training Readiness to rebound.

recommendation.title: Rest; optional 20–30-minute gentle walk
details: No running, workout or long aerobic cross-training today.
Keep any walk genuinely gentle and on flat ground.
Light mobility is fine if it does not provoke calf or medial-ankle symptoms.
recommendation.alternative: Complete rest if walking, stairs, general soreness or energy do not feel normal.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Stop the walk if posterior-tibial discomfort rises above mild awareness, changes your gait, or is worse as you continue. Do not run tomorrow if symptoms remain elevated afterward or the following morning.

signals.label: Post-marathon timing
signals.interpretation: Even with improving device scores, connective-tissue and muscular recovery lag behind headline readiness.

signals.label: Readiness rebound
signals.interpretation: Good sleep and two low-load days improved short-term recovery, but the rebound is not clearance for training.

signals.label: Acute load
signals.interpretation: Garmin now calls the load ratio optimal, yet roughly 55 km of the recent week was concentrated around the marathon.

caveats: Historical sleeping-heart-rate values were unavailable in overnight_sleep_recovery because Garmin supplied avgHeartRate under a different field name; the collector has now been corrected for future snapshots.
Wrist heart-rate data from Monday's run remain internally inconsistent (145 bpm average, 190 bpm maximum), so intensity interpretation is cautious.
Today's stress and Body Battery values are partial because the snapshot was generated mid-afternoon.

run_assessments.summary: 6.99 km at about 6:16/km, completed roughly a day after the marathon.
run_assessments.assessment: The pace was easy, but the timing made this an additional recovery cost rather than useful aerobic development. Treat its heart-rate data cautiously and allow the response to settle before the next run.

signals.label: Training load
signals.interpretation: A meaningful extra load immediately after the marathon.

signals.label: Heart rate
signals.interpretation: The maximum is inconsistent with the run and may reflect wrist-HR error or cadence lock.
